paperMetadata.title: Rethinking Model Compression and Quantization Design

abstract: In the era of deep learning, model size and computational efficiency are critical constraints for deploying neural networks on edge devices. This paper introduces a novel hybrid quantization framework that combines dynamic precision adjustment with structured pruning to maintain model performance while achieving substantial compression. We propose a precision-scaled training paradigm that dynamically adjusts bit-widths during training based on gradient sensitivity, supplemented by a block-pruning strategy that removes redundant neurons at each layer. Our approach demonstrates superior performance retention when models are compressed to 4-bit and mixed-precision representations. Experimental evaluations on the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets reveal that our method achieves up to 30% better inference speed and 25% reduction in model size over conventional techniques while maintaining accuracy within 1% of the baseline. Our contributions highlight a pathway towards efficient and scalable model deployment, especially beneficial for resource-constrained environments.

contributions.title: Dynamic Precision Adjustment
contributions.description: Introduces a novel training strategy that allows bit-widths to be adjusted dynamically during training based on the gradient sensitivity of each layer, optimizing both performance and compression.
contributions.novelty: This is the first approach that integrates gradient sensitivity into precision scaling, allowing more nuanced control over model quantization.

contributions.title: Structured Block Pruning
contributions.description: Proposes a block-pruning strategy that prunes redundant neurons layer-wise, maintaining structural integrity and reducing computational overhead significantly.
contributions.novelty: Our method uniquely focuses on block-wise pruning rather than individual neuron pruning, which preserves layer-wise feature extraction capabilities.

methodology.problemFormulation: The challenge is to compress deep neural networks to meet the resource constraints of edge devices while preserving model accuracy and inference speed.
methodology.approach: Our approach integrates dynamic bit-width adjustment with block pruning. During training, bit-widths are adjusted based on layer-wise gradient sensitivity, and pruning is applied to entire blocks of neurons deemed redundant.

components.name: Gradient Sensitivity Analyzer
components.role: Determines the appropriate bit-width for each layer during training.
components.details: Analyzes the gradient variance of each layer to determine its sensitivity and adjusts the bit-width accordingly.

components.name: Block Pruner
components.role: Reduces model size by pruning redundant neuron blocks.
components.details: Utilizes a heuristic based on neuron activity and influence on output to prune entire blocks without significant loss of accuracy.

assumptions: Layer-wise gradient variance is indicative of a layer's importance to overall model performance.
Block pruning can sufficiently reduce model size without significant accuracy loss.
limitations: The approach may not generalize well to all types of neural network architectures, particularly those with non-standard layers.
Requires substantial initial training to determine optimal block pruning configurations.

evidence.description: Evaluate the compression and accuracy retention of the proposed method on CIFAR-10.

setup.context: Testing on a standard image classification task to assess compression efficacy.
conditions: Model initially trained to baseline accuracy before applying compression techniques.

evaluation.protocol: Compare performance against baseline and state-of-the-art compression techniques.

results.notes: Achieved a 4x reduction in model size.
Achieved a 30% improvement in inference speed.

evidence.analysis: The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively compresses the model while retaining high accuracy and improving inference speed, outperforming traditional quantization methods.

works.summary: Explores post-training quantization techniques for reducing model size without retraining.

works.summary: Introduces the concept of training networks with binary weights to reduce computational load.

works.summary: Presents a comprehensive approach to model compression using pruning along with quantization.

works.reference: Hinton, G., et al. (2015). Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network.
works.summary: Discusses transferring knowledge from a large model to a smaller one while maintaining performance.

futureWork.motivation: Investigate the potential of combining multiple precision levels within a model to further optimize the trade-off between accuracy and compression.
Enhance the framework to support compression of models with non-standard architectures, such as those with dynamic layers or unconventional connectivity.
